representation.model: SmoothLocalWarpModel 4x4 normalized Gaussian basis, sigma 0.28, 8% smoothstep boundary taper
representation.per_frame_bytes: ~144 B (32 coeff floats + dims + validity + coordinate mapping + params)

device_semantics.inversion: fp32 fixed-point q_{n+1} = u - d(q_n), affine seed, max_iter 6, tol 0.001 px, safety margin 64 px
device_semantics.subdivision: implicit 21-node tree (1+4+16), 3x3 inversions per node, depth <= 2, position epsilon 0.05 internal px, area relative epsilon 0.005
device_semantics.all_or_nothing: any inversion failure, max-depth rejection or child failure discards the whole source sample, including already accepted leaves
device_semantics.invalid_model: per-sample discard (CPU oracle semantics), not a call failure
device_semantics.scatter: accepted leaves emitted through the identical polygon-rectangle clip accumulation as the affine path
device_semantics.parity: discrete decisions exact (states, contributors, masks, discards); magnitudes <= 1e-5 relative due to fp32 inversion internals

implementation_findings.band_vs_canvas_bounds: The workspace native_rows is the BAND height, but the CPU oracle bounds the inversion against the FULL canvas. First implementation passed the band height, wrongly discarding ~97% of samples on a top band. Fixed by adding canvas_width_native/canvas_height_native to ForwardDrizzleV2KernelConfig (0 = band covers the whole canvas).
implementation_findings.depth2_on_production_geometry: A 4x4 Gaussian model fitted to the full canvas always has knot spacing ~nc/3 (~1311 px), far smoother than any droplet. Depth-2 subdivision is only reachable with a compressed model domain; the production test therefore covers it with a 13x13 px domain patch inside the band plus a max-iteration inversion-stress model. Structural depth-2 acceptance is proven on the small-canvas matrix.
implementation_findings.basis_sum_degenerate: smooth_local_basis leaves raw basis weights when sum <= 1e-8; the device port mirrors factor 1.0 (not zero).
implementation_findings.nan_semantics: std::min/std::clamp NaN propagation mirrored explicitly instead of fminf/fmaxf.
